seo.metaDescription: Charts follow prefers-color-scheme and can be forced with data-ch-theme. How to connect the attribute to next-themes or to your own provider.

props.markdown: Dark mode works without any code: `tally-charts/theme.css` defines the tokens for both themes, and the charts use the dark ones when the visitor's system prefers it (`prefers-color-scheme: dark`). To follow a toggle in your app instead, set `data-ch-theme="light"` or `data-ch-theme="dark"` on `<html>` or on any ancestor of a chart. The attribute wins over the system setting, and without it the system setting decides.
The attribute works on any element, not only on `<html>`. Both panels below are pinned, so they look the same whatever the visitor's setting is:

An app whose dark mode is a class (`.dark`, as with Tailwind and shadcn) has to set the attribute too. **The class alone does not reach the tokens**, because the tokens look at `data-ch-theme` and at the system setting, not at class names.

Tell `ThemeProvider` to write both: the class for your own styles and the attribute for the charts. `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` is needed because the provider sets the attribute before React hydrates.
**next-themes is not a dependency of tally-charts.** Install it yourself (`npm i next-themes`) if you use this recipe.

Set `document.documentElement.dataset.chTheme = resolvedTheme` wherever your code toggles the class, and render the same `data-ch-theme` on `<html>` on the server, for example from a cookie, so the first paint is in the right theme and nothing flashes.
See [Theming](/docs/theming) for the tokens and [Palettes](/docs/palettes) for the vivid palette, which is light only.
